I5.quote: Atomic hydrogen (H*) has long been thought to play an important role in the dechlorination of trichloroethylene (TCE) by carbon-supported zero-valent iron (ZVI), which offers an alternative pathway for TCE dechlorination.

notes: Paper is on TCE dechlorination by S-mZVI/rGO. Hydrogen content is electrochemical or reaction-generated, not gas-phase sorbent uptake. Main, p. 2, Section 3: "All electrochemical tests were done on a Correst CS350H electrochemical workstation with 50 mM Na2SO4 as supporting electrolyte". Main, p. 5, Section 5.2, Fig. 4a: H2 accumulated as % of Fe0 "Hydrogen is produced by water corrosion of Fe0" (GC headspace, SI Text S1), i.e. H2 evolution, not uptake. Main, p. 7, Section 6, Fig. 6: CV curves in Na2SO4 identify adsorbed and absorbed H*; abstract: "The electrochemical tests confirmed the occurrence of hydrogen spillover". Code chosen: electrochemical (hydrogen electrochemistry in an electrolyte, HER and CV/Tafel). Alternative reading would be no_conditions_stated (no H2 uptake value at all); electrochemical preferred because the paper's hydrogen work is electrochemical. Not retracted (record.json is_retracted false; no retraction notice in text). Research article, so not_primary does not apply. duplicate_data does not apply.
